finding.text: The generated `ext/Chat/v3/fixture/files.jsonl` is committed (commit fd16af054), against the brief's "Never `git add` the generated `files.jsonl`". It even lists the test's deleted temp copy (`live-v3-44248.jsonl`, then `gone`). Drop it from the branch before merge.

`ChatV3.test.mjs` now writes `fixture/live-v3-<pid>.jsonl` beside the v3 fixture, but `.gitignore:232` only covers `ext/Chat/v2/fixture/live-*.jsonl`. The v3 readme's Test section says the copy is "gitignored", which is false. A killed run leaves an untracked file that the next `git add` picks up. Add `public/framework/ext/Chat/v3/fixture/live-*.jsonl` to `.gitignore`.

The partial reply is no longer cleared when its settled Reply arrives. The old `chat_line()` did `this.partial = null; this.$partial.el.remove()`, and nothing replaced it. Until the wire sends `""`, the card shows the settled Reply and the reply being written together, and every redraw of the newest card puts the partial back (`prompt()`, the `queueMicrotask(stream…)` line). The readme still says it is drawn "until its settled Reply message arrives". Either clear `partial` in `update()` when a Reply lands on the newest Prompt, or correct the readme line.
The header comment of `placement.test.mjs` says `// node ChatV3.test.mjs`; it should name `placement.test.mjs`.

`ChatV3.test.mjs` dropped the old served-tree logic (`main_tree`/`served`). It writes the live copy into the test file's own tree, so it passes only when `base` serves that same tree (the worktree's server, or the main tree after merge). Against `monorepo.localhost` from a worktree, the live checks would time out. Say this in the readme's Test line.
`core/Test/results.jsonl` (37 generated test-run lines) rides in the diff. This is harmless, but it is noise in a review diff.

Every card's muted first-words title repeats the first line of its body right under it (shots/…/1200.png, each card's top band: "Can you hear me? A second thought, no…" then "Can you hear me? A second thought, no pause."). This was the owner's earlier choice, kept as it was; it is worth a second look in step 4.
ChatV3 is a changed class, and no page shows its live instances or their state (`dirty`, `partial`, `limit`). The demo page shows only its output.
